title: Business Statistics
description: Business Statistics develops the statistical reasoning needed to make defensible decisions from variable, incomplete, and imperfect data. Students learn probability, estimation, testing, experiments, regression, forecasting, quality, reliability, risk, simulation, and communication through real cases drawn from engineered systems, manufacturing, infrastructure, human performance, aerospace testing, and biomedical measurement. The mathematical treatment is algebra-based and calculus-aware. Computation is used to deepen reasoning rather than replace it.

topics.title: Statistical Thinking, Questions, and Data Quality
topics.description: Statistics begins with a decision, not a formula. This unit teaches students to frame answerable questions, understand how data were generated, and recognize when evidence is too weak or biased for the intended decision.

children.title: Statistical problem solving
children.description: Translate an engineering, performance, health, or operational concern into a disciplined investigative cycle.

children.title: Population, sample, unit of analysis, and scope
Response, predictor, factor, treatment, and covariate
Estimand, decision threshold, and stakeholder consequence
Data types and structures
children.description: Identify the structure of a dataset because valid summaries and models depend on what each row, column, and time index represents.

children.title: Categorical, ordinal, count, and continuous variables
Cross-sectional, longitudinal, time-series, and spatial data
Independent, paired, clustered, and repeated observations
Wide versus tidy data and data dictionaries
Data provenance and quality
children.description: Audit the chain from measurement to analysis before treating a spreadsheet as evidence.

children.title: Units, metadata, calibration, and source lineage
Missingness, duplicates, impossible values, and range checks
Measurement error, rounding, censoring, and detection limits
Selection, nonresponse, survivorship, and convenience bias
Statistical versus practical importance

children.title: Baseline risk and absolute versus relative change
Engineering tolerance or minimal important difference

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics and Exploratory Visualization
topics.description: Exploration makes variation visible before formal modeling begins. Students learn to summarize distributions and relationships without hiding skew, subgroups, anomalies, or uncertainty.

children.title: Center, spread, and position
children.description: Describe a distribution with summaries suited to its scale and shape.

children.title: Mean, median, mode, and weighted mean
Range, variance, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation
Distribution displays
children.description: Choose graphics that reveal shape, outliers, and sample size rather than merely decorate a report.

children.title: Dotplots, histograms, density displays, and empirical CDFs
Bin width, axis integrity, and perceptual pitfalls
Relationships and grouped comparisons
children.description: Explore how outcomes vary with predictors, groups, and operating conditions.

children.title: Communicating exploratory findings
children.description: Turn exploratory work into a concise statement of pattern, exception, and next question.

children.title: Outlier investigation rather than automatic deletion

topics.title: Probability, Conditional Reasoning, and Bayesian Updating
topics.description: Probability provides a language for uncertain events and incomplete information. It supports risk assessment, diagnosis, reliability, quality, forecasting, and rational updating when new evidence arrives.

children.title: Probability foundations
children.description: Build coherent event models and combine events without double counting.

children.title: Complements, unions, intersections, and mutually exclusive events
Conditional probability and independence
children.description: Reason about evidence, screening, failure modes, and subgroup risk.

children.title: Bayes' theorem
children.description: Update a prior probability using the diagnostic or predictive value of observed evidence.

children.title: Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and prevalence
Engineering fault diagnosis and biomedical testing examples
Expected value and decision criteria
children.description: Compare uncertain choices using consequences as well as probabilities.

children.title: Expected value, expected loss, and utility awareness
Risk attitude, safety constraints, and tail consequences

topics.title: Random Variables and Probability Distributions
topics.description: Probability distributions convert uncertain quantities into models that can be calculated, simulated, checked, and used for design. Students learn both the usefulness and the limits of standard distribution families.

children.title: Random variables and moments
children.description: Represent uncertain numerical outcomes and summarize their long-run behavior.

children.title: Discrete distributions
children.description: Model binary outcomes, counts, defects, arrivals, and rare events.

children.title: Continuous distributions
children.description: Model measurements, waiting times, lifetimes, and positive skew.

children.title: Uniform, normal, and standard normal distributions
Model selection and checking
children.description: Treat a named distribution as a testable approximation rather than a fact.

children.title: Support, shape, parameter meaning, and generative mechanism

topics.title: Joint Distributions, Covariance, Sampling, and the Central Limit Theorem
topics.description: This unit connects individual observations to sample statistics. It explains dependence, sampling variability, and why repeated samples, not a single convenient dataset, govern the reliability of conclusions.

children.title: Joint behavior and dependence
children.description: Describe how two uncertain quantities vary together.

children.title: Sums and linear combinations of random variables
Sampling designs
children.description: Choose a sampling method that supports the intended population claim.

children.title: Simple random, systematic, stratified, and cluster sampling
Coverage, nonresponse, attrition, and weighting awareness
Sampling distributions and standard error
children.description: Understand that an estimate changes from sample to sample.

children.title: Sampling distribution of a mean and proportion
Design effects from clustering and dependence
Central limit theorem and simulation
children.description: Use asymptotic reasoning responsibly and verify it when samples are small, skewed, or dependent.

children.title: Law of large numbers versus central limit theorem
Role of sample size and population shape
Monte Carlo demonstration of repeated sampling
Limits under heavy tails, dependence, and selection bias

topics.title: Estimation, Confidence Intervals, and Resampling
topics.description: Estimation replaces false precision with a defensible range. Students learn to quantify uncertainty, plan precision, and use resampling when textbook formulas are fragile or unavailable.

children.title: Point estimation
children.description: Select and evaluate estimators for means, proportions, differences, and model parameters.

children.title: Bias, variability, and mean squared error intuition
Confidence intervals
children.description: Construct and interpret intervals without claiming that confidence is the probability a fixed parameter lies inside one realized interval.

children.title: Confidence level and margin of error
Intervals for means, proportions, and differences
Precision and sample-size planning
children.description: Balance desired precision, variability, cost, attrition, and feasibility before collecting data.

children.title: Pilot estimates and conservative planning values
Bootstrap and resampling
children.description: Approximate sampling uncertainty by repeatedly resampling observed data.

children.title: Failure modes with tiny or unrepresentative samples

topics.title: Hypothesis Tests, Effect Sizes, Power, and Multiplicity
topics.description: Hypothesis testing is a structured way to measure incompatibility between data and a null model, not a truth machine. The unit emphasizes effect magnitude, uncertainty, assumptions, and the costs of wrong decisions.

children.title: Testing framework
children.description: Form hypotheses and interpret test evidence in the context of a real decision.

children.title: Test statistic, reference distribution, and p-value
Type I and Type II errors
Core tests
children.description: Apply common tests to means, proportions, and paired changes.

children.title: Effect sizes and practical significance
children.description: Report how large an effect is and whether that magnitude matters.

children.title: Risk ratio, odds ratio, and number-needed-to-treat awareness
Power and multiplicity
children.description: Design adequately informative studies and control overclaiming when many questions are tested.

children.title: Power, sample size, variability, and effect size
Preregistration, stopping rules, and selective reporting

topics.title: Experimental Design, A/B Tests, and Causal Reasoning
topics.description: Well-designed experiments create evidence about cause rather than mere association. Students learn to design efficient comparisons and recognize where causal claims fail in observational data.

children.title: Principles of designed experiments
children.description: Use design to separate treatment effects from noise and nuisance variation.

children.title: Blinding and placebo/sham controls where relevant
A/B and randomized trials
children.description: Plan and analyze two-condition interventions in digital, operational, engineering, and health settings.

children.title: Compliance, attrition, contamination, and intention-to-treat awareness
Power, duration, peeking, and novelty effects
Factorial and response-surface foundations
children.description: Study several factors efficiently and detect when their effects depend on one another.

children.title: Observational causal reasoning
children.description: Avoid converting regression adjustment into an automatic causal claim.

children.title: Causal diagrams at an introductory level
Sensitivity, assumptions, and limits of transportability

topics.title: ANOVA, Categorical Data, and Nonparametric Methods
topics.description: Many real studies compare more than two groups, use categorical outcomes, or violate simple normal-model assumptions. This unit expands the toolkit while keeping the scientific question primary.

children.title: Analysis of variance
children.description: Partition variation to compare several group means within one coherent model.

children.title: Planned contrasts and multiplicity-aware post-hoc comparisons
Contingency-table methods
children.description: Analyze association and fit for categorical outcomes.

children.title: Fisher exact test awareness and standardized residuals
Nonparametric and robust methods
children.description: Use rank-based or permutation approaches when scale, shape, or outliers undermine mean-based procedures.

children.title: Repeated and clustered comparisons
children.description: Recognize dependence that ordinary group tests cannot ignore.

children.title: Mixed-effects model as a forward bridge

topics.title: Correlation, Linear Regression, and Model Diagnostics
topics.description: Regression turns relationships into explicit quantitative models for explanation, calibration, and prediction. Students learn to interpret coefficients, examine residuals, and resist causal or extrapolative overreach.

children.title: Correlation and simple regression

children.title: Slope, intercept, fitted value, and residual
Multiple regression

children.title: Statistical inference for regression
children.description: Quantify uncertainty in coefficients and predictions.

children.title: Prediction interval for a new observation

Diagnostics and remedial action

children.title: Linearity, independence, constant variance, and residual shape

topics.title: Prediction, Classification, and Model Validation
topics.description: A model that explains past data may still fail on new cases. This unit introduces honest validation, baseline comparisons, classification, and the distinction between predictive usefulness and scientific explanation.

children.title: Prediction workflow

children.title: Validation and generalization
children.description: Estimate performance on unseen data and detect overfitting.

children.title: Classification foundations

children.title: Confusion matrix, sensitivity, specificity, and precision

topics.title: Time Series, Forecasting, and Statistical Process Monitoring
topics.description: Time ordering creates dependence that ordinary cross-sectional methods miss. Students learn to forecast responsibly, evaluate forecasts against honest baselines, and distinguish common-cause variation from a process change.

Separated inputs, transformations, models, and outputs
